hook: Tomorrow, G T A 6 comes out. Benny pays about eighty dollars. The cashier calls it a bargain.
angle: Counter-intuitive: $79.99 feels $20 more than GTA 5's $59.99, but in today's money GTA 5 cost about $86, so GTA 6 is about $6 cheaper.

facts.claim: GTA V launched Sept 2013 at US standard price $59.99 (about $86 adjusted to today's money using BLS CPI-U).

twist: The 'expensive' game is cheaper than GTA 5 was after inflation.
open_loop: Why does the cashier call about $80 a bargain? Paid off in lines 5-7.
payoff: About $86 then vs about $80 now: about $6 cheaper.
ab_ending: A: Worth it / B: Too much. Splits opinion; the real-terms math does not settle affordability.
ip_notes: No Rockstar characters, logos, footage, art, music. 'GTA 6' plain text. Cashier is Benny's generic hooded stranger.
math: 59.99 x 337.511 / 234.149 = 86.47 -> 'about 86' (Sep 2026 CPI 336.940 gives 86.33, also about 86). 86.47 - 79.99 = 6.48 -> 'about 6'; on screen ~$86, ~$80, ~$6 using the same rounded figures (86 - 80 = 6). Voice 'about eighty/sixty/eighty-six/six' = screen '~$80/~$60/~$86/~$6'.
unverified: GTA 5 $59.99 launch price is from one outlet I opened (GG Recon); other search snippets agree but I did not open them
September 2026 CPI 336.940 is from a secondary site; October 2026 337.511 is from the BLS release I opened (either gives about $86)
Inflation-adjusted price is not affordability (wages), and CPI is the all-items index, not a games price index
Standard $79.99 relies on GameLuster, an outlet, not Rockstar's own page
notes_for_scriptwriter: Keep 'about' in voice and '~' on screen. Money outfit. Not financial advice in description.
